An operator's act: an agent may name a space it was granted and may never open one.

params.name: name
params.description: 1-64 characters, starting alphanumeric, then letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore

params.name: owner
params.description: who owns it; default the calling identity

params.name: policy
params.description: its review policy; default `inherit` — this deployment's configured policy. ADR-0023 d1 requires a space to carry one and names no vocabulary, so the string is stored verbatim

verbs.returns: object: {name, owner, policy, created, event_id} — or the existing row with `duplicate: true`

errors.-32602: a name outside the charset, or a role below admin

verbs.name: dg.spaces
verbs.summary: The store's partitions (ADR-0023 d1): every declared space with its owner, its review policy and how many artifacts sit in it (below the reviewer role, how many the caller may read: the promoted rows and its own, in a space it holds `read` on, and its own anywhere), `granted`, the capabilities the caller holds there (ADR-0115 d6; every one for an admin), and which space a write defaults to. `unregistered` names spaces the store holds rows in that nothing declared — empty on a deployment this daemon has started, because startup registers exactly those. Names and counts, never content: this is a directory, not a read.
verbs.returns: object: {default, spaces[{name, owner, policy, artifacts, granted[], event_id, identity, ts, builtin?}], unregistered[]}

verbs.name: dg.status
verbs.summary: Queue depths, journal tip, gate budget, role-specific gauges — or one artifact's lifecycle row. Below the reviewer role `queues`, `replacements` and `runs` count only the rows the caller may read: the promoted rows and its own (INV-SEC-10), and `tip`, the journal's newest event, is null (GAPS 158). From the reviewer role up it carries `caps[]`, every cap that pauses a pass, `{setting, words, spent, limit, unit, day, resets_at}`, counted in the daemon's own process on its own clock, and `paused[]`, `{pass, cause, words, since, until?, cap?}` for each pass (grade, second_opinion, settle, re_review) that stopped on its last tick, cause `cap` or `backend` (ADR-0132 d5, d18). An API key of scope `events` is answered `{paused, caps, now}` alone (d6). `deployment {mode, in_file, why, since}` is the mode the gate resolved, the file's value (null when the line is absent), the first condition that keeps a file that says development out of it, and the time of the journal's last `deployment-mode`, null when it holds none (ADR-0135 d1). `now` is the daemon's clock in epoch milliseconds, the one every event's ts is stamped on, on every answer, an events key's and one row's included (ADR-0139 d6). From the reviewer role up, `grade_again {stale, oldest, per_tick}` is what the last grade pass left to grade again: the held claims graded before the grading in force for their kind, the oldest one's state ts, and `[gating].grade_again_per_tick` (ADR-0139 d2). To a caller who reads every space, `routing {open[{question, space, crew, wait_minutes, minutes_left, starts, held_clock}], held_sheets[{artifact_id, space, code, crew}], only_admin_proposed[{group_id, space, proposer}], starts_file}` is what doctor's questions and crews lines read: each question still with its answering crew, how many daemon starts restarted its count and whether its wait ran while the served clock was held, each held crew sheet the routing refuses, and each widening crew sheet version only its proposer, the one admin, could commit, and why routing-starts.json could not be read or written, null when it could (ADR-0143 d1, d8; GAPS 1386, 1391). Below the reviewer role the envelope's `derives_from` names only the parents the caller may read, and `derives_from_withheld`, present when any is left out, counts the rest (GAPS 156).

params.name: artifact_id
params.description: one artifact instead of the deployment

verbs.returns: object

verbs.name: dg.upload
verbs.summary: Open or resume the caller's upload of one file before the dg.ingest that binds it (ADR-0126 d3; 24 — Attachments §3): a PNG, JPEG or WebP image up to 7 MiB, or a PDF up to 16 MiB, keyed by the caller and the file's SHA-256, so a second call answers the recorded offset. An upload is no content: no event names it, nobody but its uploader addresses it, and it is removed when it expires. Bytes another claim holds start a fresh upload. Refused when the caller may contribute nowhere. Writer identity is the connection's (I2).

params.name: sha256
params.description: the file's SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex

params.name: size_bytes
params.description: the file's exact length

params.name: media_type
params.description: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or application/pdf; checked against the magic bytes at the last part

params.name: name
params.description: 1 to 255 UTF-8 bytes, no control character, slash, backslash or NUL; display only, never a file name on disk

verbs.returns: object: {upload_id, offset, size_bytes, part_bytes: 524288, complete, expires_at}

errors.-32602: data.reason media_type, attachment_too_large, upload_conflict, attachment_name or not_granted, each with its sentence (24 §3.1)
errors.-32015: attachment storage at its bound: data.reason upload_quota (with data.retry_after_ms until the caller's oldest upload expires) or attachment_budget (a review frees it)

verbs.name: dg.upload_part
verbs.summary: One part of the caller's open upload at the recorded offset, strict base64 of 1 to 524,288 bytes (24 §3). The last part re-hashes the file and checks its magic bytes, frames, sides and encryption; bytes that can never bind are removed and the sentence says so (GAPS 493). Another identity's upload id is answered as unknown.

params.name: upload_id
params.description: from dg.upload

params.name: offset
params.description: the recorded offset dg.upload or the last part answered

params.name: content
params.description: the part, strict base64

verbs.returns: object: {offset}; on the last part {offset, complete: true, sha256}

errors.-32602: data.reason upload_unknown, encoding, part_offset (data.recorded), part_size, hash_mismatch, media_mismatch, animated, image_dimensions or pdf_encrypted, each with its sentence (24 §3.1)

verbs.summary: Walk the journal chain and verify every signature. Below the reviewer role `events` counts the events the caller may read, as dg.events serves them, and `tip` names the last of them (GAPS 158).
verbs.returns: object: {events, tip}

verbs.name: dg.who_can_sign
verbs.summary: Who may sign a held row, or a row of a kind the caller would write (ADR-0134 d3): the people who hold reviewer or admin and read on its space, never its writer, by name to an admin and by letter (A, B, ... in the people file's order) to anyone else, and the graders whose promote can count toward its k under the review mode and its class, each by its backend's words. In development the developer comes first on their own row with `self_signs`, and no demo person is listed on it; outside development no demo person is listed (ADR-0135 d2, d5). Refused to every API key, whatever its role or scope.

params.description: a held row; exactly one of artifact_id and content_type

params.name: space

verbs.returns: object: {people[{who, role, `you?`, self_signs?}], graders[{label, provider}], enough, words, notify} — `enough` is whether those listed can bring the row to its k with no one else, read through the count the auto pass reads; `words` the sentence a console prints; `notify` whether an events key reads the space, so an ask reaches a sink

verbs.name: dg.why
verbs.summary: Every signed event about one artifact, in order — the provenance answer, with `self_signed` and `demo_signed`, whether its promotion rested on its author's or a demo person's signature (ADR-0135 d3). A reviewer may also name a journal key that is no row (a work area's, a group's); below the reviewer role only a row the caller may read is answered, and a payload's id of a row the caller may not read is null (GAPS 156).
verbs.returns: object: {artifact_id, producer, events[]} — `producer` is the row's, off its first ingest, null when it named none (ADR-0107 d1)

errors.-32602: unknown artifact: <the id's first 16 characters> — an id that names no row, and, below the reviewer role, a row the caller may not read: another identity's row that is not promoted, answered exactly as an id that names nothing

verbs.name: dg.workarea
verbs.summary: The caller's own work area from the inside (ADR-0102 d8): its own rows with their state, the promoted rows in it whoever wrote them, counts over those two by state, and the caller's own open or complete state. Another identity's rows that are not promoted are never in it, nor counted (ADR-0053, INV-SEC-10). The caller's recorded rows are evidence and are counted apart. Metadata only — ids, states and kinds, never content. The identity is the connection's (I2).

params.name: workarea
params.description: the work area, by its path

params.name: space
params.description: default main; must already exist

verbs.returns: object: {space, name, state: open|complete, counts{state: n}, rows[{artifact_id, state, kind, held, trust_class, producer}], recorded, producers[{name, kind, rows}]} — `producers` counts the rows shown by the producer each names (ADR-0107 d1)

errors.-32602: an unknown space, a name outside the grammar, or a work area the caller never wrote into — the same answer whether or not another identity did

verbs.name: dg.workarea_relate
verbs.summary: Relate one work area to another in the same space (ADR-0107 d2): `opened_by` (this area was opened by work in target: a subagent's area under its orchestrator's), `continues` (this area carries on target, which is complete) or `derived_from` (this area's work derives from target's promoted rows). The gate signs a `workarea-related` event under its own key, naming the caller as `by`. It changes no visibility, decides nothing and ranks nothing. An agent relates only an area it wrote into, to an area it wrote into or that holds a promoted row; a reviewer or an admin relates any area someone wrote into. A cycle, a missing target and a `continues` whose target is not complete are refused; the same relation again answers `changed: false` and journals nothing. `lift: true` withdraws a relation with a second event and is a reviewer's: nothing erases one.

params.name: workarea
params.description: the area that depends, by its path

params.name: kind
params.description: how it relates to target (ADR-0107 d2)

params.name: target
params.description: the area it depends on, in the same space

params.name: space
params.description: default main; must already exist. Both areas are in it: cross-space lineage stays claim-level derives_from (ADR-0035 d1)

params.name: note
params.description: why, for the journal

params.name: producer
params.description: what produced this write, in the writer's own words (ADR-0107 d1): {name, kind}, kind one of agent, hook, person, tool and name one segment of the work-area grammar. Read by people and never checked as an authorization; the identity stays the connection's (I2). Rides the ingest event beside the work area, never the envelope, so it changes no artifact id

params.name: lift
params.description: reviewer and admin only: withdraw the relation with a second event; a lift of a relation not in effect answers `changed: false`
